import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Initialize the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a bubble chart to show multiple dimensions
# X-axis: Price, Y-axis: Megapixels
# Hue (Color): Brand
# Size: Max ISO (a measure of sensor sensitivity)
# Style (Marker): Body Type

    data=df,
    x="price_usd",
    y="megapixels",
    hue="brand",
    size="max_iso",
    style="body_type",
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Range of bubble sizes
    palette="viridis",
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# Add annotations for each data point for better clarity
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(
        row['price_usd'],
        row['megapixels'] + 1.5, # Offset text above the bubble
        f"{row['brand']} '{str(row['model_year'])[-2:]}\n{row['sensor_type']}",
        fontdict={'size': 10, 'color': 'black', 'weight': 'semibold'},
        ha='center' # Center align horizontally
    )
